newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares shake off doldrums, set record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares shake off doldrums, set record.

text.p: Swiss shares powered to their eighth consecutive record close on Monday after overcoming a tentative start.
Firming bond prices gave shares a boost, dealers said. In the current bullish environment, even laggards such as stocks of Swiss retailers saw interest, one dealer said.
But some traders thought a correction could not be ruled out in the near future.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 26.4 points, or 0.61 percent, at 4,384.3 points after touching an all-time high of 4,389.5 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) climbed 12.88 points, or 0.46 percent, to 2,796.13.
Trade was heavily influenced by derivatives-linked transactions. Volume was high but was below last week's levels.
Roche certificates were actively sought by U.S. and British investors, one dealer said. The stock jumped 245 francs to 12,435.
Novartis registered shares gained nine francs to 1,702. Many investors were buying Novartis to get subscription rights for Ciba Specialty Chemicals, a Novartis subsidiary which will soon be spun off.
Banks mostly consolidated recent gains. Credit Suisse Group lost 1.50 francs to 149.50. SBC gave up one franc to 276.50 francs. UBS bearers were off 10 francs to end at 1,239.
Traders said technicals factors and insecurity stemming from the debate about possible Swiss bank accounts of Holocaust victims were behind the banks' weakness.
Insurers Swiss Re and Baloise were in demand.
Among industrials, ABB, Alusuisse, Holderbank and Sulzer gained ground. Alusuisse jumped 15 francs to 1,209. The company will hold its annual news conference on Tuesday.
